common_name: Deep Impact Daylily (Golden Patterned R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Deep Impact is a fragrant, ruffled patterned daylily that reblooms through the season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Deep Impact, registered by hybridizer Peroni, is a bright golden-yellow patterned daylily with a deep maroon eyezone and a matching yellow appliqué pattern in the throat, carried on ruffled, fragrant, reblooming flowers. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2024, an award honoring the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year, a distinct category from the eyed/banded-focused Don C. Stevens Award. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and bud count.

common_name: Wacky Wednesday Daylily (Purple-Streaked R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Wacky Wednesday shows a distinctive streaked pattern on every bloom, a genuinely unusual trait among patterned daylilies.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Wacky Wednesday, registered by hybridizer Elaine Seifert, is a purple daylily with striking white streaking across the petals and a chartreuse throat, with the streaked pattern appearing consistently on every bloom rather than as an occasional sport. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2023, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Four Beasts in One Daylily (Lemon Patterned R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Four Beasts in One carries a plum-cream pattern over its lemon yellow base color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Four Beasts in One, registered by hybridizer Di DeCaire, is a lemon-yellow self daylily patterned with a plum-and-cream design across the petals, an unusual combination for the patterned-daylily category. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2022, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and bud count.

common_name: Yankee Pinstripes Daylily (Lavender Striped R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Yankee Pinstripes shows white striping over darker segments, a distinctive broken-color pattern.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Yankee Pinstripes, registered by hybridizer Richard Howard, is a lavender broken-color blend daylily with darker segments and distinctive white striping over a yellow throat, giving the bloom a pinstriped appearance that inspired its name. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2021, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Katisue Herrington Daylily (Fuchsia Crispate Unusual-Form R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Katisue Herrington is a crispate unusual-form daylily with striking veined coloring.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Katisue Herrington, registered by hybridizer Heather Herrington, is a fuchsia orchid-rose blend unusual-form daylily with darker veining, a neon lime-green throat, and a cream petal edge, displaying the twisted, pinched crispate form prized in this daylily class. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2020, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and form.

common_name: Almira Buffalo Bone Jackson Daylily (Cream Veined-Eye R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Almira Buffalo Bone Jackson carries a soft purple veined eye over cream petals edged in a thin double line.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Almira Buffalo Bone Jackson, registered by hybridizer Robert A. Faulkner, is a light cream daylily marked with a large, soft purple, veined eyezone and a thin double-line edge, a quietly elegant pattern within the patterned-daylily class. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2018, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and eye definition.

common_name: Alien DNA Daylily (Lavender-Raspberry Appliqué R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Alien DNA carries a distinctive appliquéd patterned green heart throat beneath darker veining.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Alien DNA, registered by hybridizer Robert P. Selman, is a lavender-raspberry bitone daylily with darker veining and a distinctive appliquéd, patterned green throat shaped like a heart, giving the bloom unusual visual depth. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2017, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and pattern definition.

common_name: Get Jiggy Daylily (Cream Multi-Banded R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Get Jiggy shows a multi-banded violet eye above a green throat.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Get Jiggy, registered by hybridizer Patrick Stamile, is a cream daylily with a multi-banded violet eyezone layered above a green throat, a complex patterned design from one of the most prolific American daylily breeders. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2016, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and pattern clarity.

common_name: Jessica Lynn Bell Daylily (R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Jessica Lynn Bell, registered by hybridizer Tim Bell and named for the hybridizer's daughter, won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2015, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. As with all daylilies in this award class, the bloom displays a distinctive color pattern beyond a simple eye or band, the defining trait that sets Munson Award winners apart from the related Don C. Stevens Award for eyed and banded cultivars. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Catcher in the Eye Daylily (Lavender-Purple Picotee R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Catcher in the Eye carries a purple eye with a contrasting picotee edge.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Catcher in the Eye, registered by hybridizer John L. Kinnebrew Jr., is a lavender-purple daylily with a bold purple eyezone and a contrasting picotee edge over a yellow throat. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2008, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and eye definition.

common_name: Gerda Brooker Daylily (Cream Triple-Eye R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Gerda Brooker shows an unusual triple-layered eye pattern, rarer than the simple single eye common to most eyed daylilies.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Gerda Brooker, registered by hybridizer Morss, is a cream daylily patterned with a triple eye of lavender-lilac, bordered by red-violet edges and veins above a yellow-green throat, an unusually complex layered pattern for its era. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2005, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and pattern clarity.

common_name: Tune the Harp Daylily (Cream-Lavender Ruffled R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Tune the Harp carries light purple ruffles over a cream-lavender base.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Tune the Harp, registered by hybridizer Ra Hansen, is a cream-lavender daylily with light purple ruffled petal edges, a softer and more subtly patterned entry among R.W. Munson, Jr. Award winners. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2004, recognizing the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and ruffle definition.

common_name: Witch Stitchery Daylily (Cream Purple-Edged R.W. Munson Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Witch Stitchery carries a double-layered lavender-and-purple edge, part of the inaugural class of R.W. Munson, Jr. Award winners.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Witch Stitchery, registered by hybridizer Morss, is a cream daylily edged in lavender and bordered again in purple over a green throat, part of the inaugural class of winners when the American Hemerocallis Society established the R.W. Munson, Jr. Award in 2001 to recognize the most outstanding patterned daylily of the year. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering and edge definition.
